newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Dec 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Dec 31.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

SING TAO -- Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping's health deteriorated last week and he was sent to hospital. Some people said China Central Television's decision to air a documentary about Deng was related to his health condition, because in the history of the Communist Party, life stories of top leaders were seldom broadcast when they were alive.

-- APPLE DAILY -- Chinese democratic activist Chai Ling was on a "blacklist" of the Hong Kong Government and was banned from entering the territory. Chai applied to the British Consulate in New York for a visa to come to Hong Kong for a visit but was told she was on a blacklist and her application was rejected.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- The law governing the Hong Kong garrison of the People's Liberation Army had been passed by China's National People's Congress.
-- Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen talked about international political developments and China's diplomatic achievements.
-- MING PAO -- The mastermind of a Guangzhou gang of robbers who had stolen more than one million yuan and who were recently captured turned out to be a 14-year-old boy.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Financial Secretary Donald Tsang said he was confident he could stay in his present post after the handover. He would talk about the financial budget for the next half of 1997 when meeting Tung on Tuesday.

-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- China International Trust & Investment Corp (CITIC) announced the sale of 15.47 per cent of its shares in its associate CITIC Pacific to CITIC Pacific Chairman Larry Yung and several senior executives, which meant Yung had successfully consolidated his control over CITIC Pacific.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Henderson Land Development, one of the territory's largest developers, planned to become the first Hong Kong company to list in Tokyo.
-- Chase Manhattan Bank said the mortgage war was ending and the rate was likely to settle at 0.5 percent over prime.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- A Chinese official said China's housing crisis should be an issue of international concern, which needed increased overseas investment.
